root_cause.text: Concurrent updates to multiple bitfields (`is_open`, `has_lease`, `on_list`) that share the same byte in `struct cached_fid` cause data races because bitfield assignments use byte-level read-modify-write operations, allowing one update to inadvertently restore stale values of other flags.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly describes the problem: "is_open, has_lease and on_list are stored in the same bitfield byte in struct cached_fid but are updated in different code paths that may run concurrently. Bitfield assignments generate byte read–modify–write operations ... so updating one flag can restore stale values of the others." The patch resolves this by converting the bitfields to separate `bool` fields.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential issues with bitfield usage on booleans by making them full-width bool members.
intent_record.what: Removed the `:1` bitfield width specifier from four `bool` members (`has_lease`, `is_open`, `on_list`, `file_all_info_is_valid`) in the `cached_fid` structure.
intent_record.how: Each member now occupies a full byte (or alignment unit) instead of a single bit, increasing the structure size and eliminating any bitfield packing behavior. The members are now regular booleans, which allows taking their addresses, avoids potential compiler- or architecture-specific bitfield pitfalls (e.g., ordering, atomic access), and ensures they can be used with standard atomic operations.
